primitives.name: Object Decomposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: To address this, GenMOJO decomposes the scene into individual objects, optimizing a differentiable set of deformable Gaussians per object.
primitives.assumptions: Scene contains distinct foreground objects and background; each object can be modeled as a set of deformable 3D Gaussians.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when objects are not clearly segmented or overlap significantly without clear foreground/background distinction.

layer2.mapping: Each object's Gaussian representation maps to a probabilistic latent space in GSI, enabling modular inference of object states.
layer2.telemetry: Segmentation accuracy and object-wise Gaussian convergence metrics.

primitives.name: Gaussian Splatting
primitives.verbatim_quote: It performs joint Gaussian splatting to render the full scene, capturing cross-object occlusions, and enabling occlusion-aware supervision.
primitives.assumptions: Scene geometry can be represented as a union of 3D Gaussians; rendering is differentiable and supports occlusion modeling.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when occlusions are too complex or when Gaussians fail to capture high-frequency geometric details.

layer2.mapping: Joint splatting kernel encodes spatial and temporal dependencies across objects, enabling GSE to compute consistent point tracks.
layer2.telemetry: Rendered image fidelity and point track consistency under novel viewpoints.

primitives.name: Coordinate Transformation
primitives.verbatim_quote: To bridge the gap between object-centric priors and the global frame-centric coordinate system of videos, GenMOJO uses differentiable transformations that align generative and rendering constraints within a unified framework.
primitives.assumptions: Object poses and camera trajectories are known; transformations are smooth and invertible across timesteps.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when camera motion is highly non-rigid or when object poses are ambiguous.

layer2.mapping: Differentiable transformation maps object-centric Gaussians into scene coordinates, enabling GSI to unify local priors into global scene beliefs.
layer2.telemetry: Transformation smoothness and alignment error between rendered and observed frames.

GenMOJO operates under the principle that 4D scene reconstruction from monocular video requires both object-level generative priors and global rendering consistency. The core innovation lies in decomposing the scene into individual objects, each represented by a set of deformable 3D Gaussians. These Gaussians are optimized using object-centric Score Distillation Sampling (SDS), which leverages pre-trained diffusion models to generate plausible object appearances. Subsequently, a joint Gaussian splatting process renders the full scene, incorporating cross-object occlusions through rendering loss functions on instance masks, depth, and RGB. A key technical advancement is the use of differentiable transformations to map object-centric Gaussians into a shared scene coordinate frame. This alignment ensures that generative priors and rendering constraints cohere within a unified framework. The method thus bridges the gap between object-centric perception and frame-centric rendering, enabling robust 4D scene recovery even in cluttered environments with heavy occlusions. Failure modes include missegmentation of objects, inaccurate pose estimation, and insufficient modeling of complex occlusion dynamics.
